items.title: Establish the governed Figma libraries and component contribution model
items.outcome: Android, web and admin designers publish from governed foundation and component libraries with explicit ownership, contribution, versioning, deprecation and platform-variant rules.
items.context: Tokens alone do not prevent duplicate components or breaking visual changes. A large team needs a library API and contribution workflow before feature files multiply.
scope: Foundation, shared semantic component and platform-variant library boundaries
Component naming, properties, variants, slots, content limits, descriptions and status
Contribution request, review, test, release, deprecation and migration flow
Semantic versioning, release notes, dependency update and rollback
CDO major-release and Design Systems Lead minor-release decision rights
acceptance_criteria: Every published component has an owner, description, property contract, accessibility behavior and supported platforms
A local duplicate of a published semantic component is rejected by review and registry lint
Breaking token or component changes require a major version, migration plan and CDO approval
Deprecated components name a replacement and removal version and remain available through migration
Figma permissions prevent feature squads from publishing directly to shared libraries
contracts_schema: Library, component, property, platform variant, version, status, replacement and owner records referenced by T-UXR-06
security_privacy: Library examples contain synthetic values and no production screenshots
External library access and asset export are auditable and revoked on offboarding
observability: Library adoption, duplicate component, deprecated instance, review age and version lag by platform
tests: Duplicate semantic component and missing owner rejection
rollout_rollback: Publish empty governed shells before component work; existing drafts import as unpublished candidates
Rollback unpublishes a bad version and restores the prior library without deleting dependent instances
non_goals: One component implementation shared unchanged across platforms
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and governed Figma libraries. Design Systems owns shared files; platform squads contribute through isolated branches and review requests.
definition_of_done: Library topology and contribution contract operational
Design Systems, DesignOps, Accessibility, UX Engineering and CDO approvals recorded
Versioning, permission and duplicate tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Define typography, iconography, illustration and financial visual language
items.outcome: The selected direction becomes a legible, culturally appropriate and platform-adaptable type, icon, illustration and financial-notation system rather than a mood board.
items.context: Finance screens depend on dense numbers, uncertainty and status. Decorative identity that weakens numeral distinction, localization or platform recognition is a correctness defect.
scope: UI type roles, tabular numerals, currency, percentages, dates, hierarchy and long-form explanation
Icon grid, stroke/fill rules, metaphors, labels and platform adaptation
Illustration purpose, subject boundaries, synthetic-data treatment and asset production
Financial notation for positive, negative, projected, pending, stale, reversed, shared and redacted values
Light, dark and high-contrast examples across Android, web and admin
acceptance_criteria: Amounts, decimal positions, signs, currencies and dates remain unambiguous at minimum supported size
Icons never carry a critical action or state without text or accessible naming
Projected, stale, pending and confirmed values remain distinguishable without color
Type and illustration survive pseudo-localization, 200 percent zoom and largest Android text scale
The CDO and Accessibility Lead approve the system against representative debt, transaction and operator screens
contracts_schema: Typography, icon, illustration and financial-notation asset roles extend T-DSY-01 semantic tokens
security_privacy: No illustration or example implies guaranteed payoff, investment advice or unsafe household access
Assets carry no real financial or participant data
observability: Unmapped icon, non-tabular financial numeral, asset version and pseudo-localization defect counts
tests: Numeral ambiguity and no-color state tests
Icon name and text-equivalent coverage lint
rollout_rollback: Publish as a versioned foundation release consumed by component tickets
Rollback restores prior assets and token aliases while affected screens migrate
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and foundations library. Type, icon and illustration subteams own non-overlapping asset pages under one CDO direction.
definition_of_done: Foundation assets and usage guidance published
License, accessibility, localization and platform reviews pass
Representative screen applications approved by CDO
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Design navigation, action, form and validation component families
items.outcome: Platform squads assemble navigation and input-heavy financial journeys from tested semantic components instead of inventing controls, validation and focus behavior per screen.
items.context: Debt, transaction, billing and admin workflows contain high-risk numeric and destructive inputs. Missing states or inconsistent validation create financial errors and inaccessible dead ends.
scope: App bars, navigation bar/rail/drawer, side navigation, breadcrumbs, tabs, steppers and deep-link landing
Buttons, icon actions, menus, FAB policy, links and destructive actions
Text, number, money, rate, date, select, autocomplete, checkbox, radio, switch, slider, OTP/passkey and file inputs
Inline validation, help, required/optional, units, min/max, conflict and server-error behavior
Android Material, responsive web and dense admin variants
acceptance_criteria: Every interactive component covers default, focus, active, selected, disabled, loading and error where applicable
Money/rate inputs show units, accepted precision, bounds and server normalization before submission
All actions are keyboard/switch reachable and Android targets meet 48dp with spacing
Destructive actions show consequence, scope and recovery and never rely on a generic confirmation
Navigation components adapt structurally across compact, expanded and narrow web layouts
contracts_schema: Component property and validation-state contracts map to API error codes and T-UX-01 state IDs
security_privacy: Credential, key and recovery inputs never expose values in examples, analytics or error copy
Denied controls do not reveal hidden resource existence
observability: Validation error, abandoned form, focus trap, inaccessible target and duplicate component counts
tests: Keyboard, focus, screen-reader and Android target-size specifications
Money/rate boundary and server-error mapping fixtures
rollout_rollback: Publish additive component versions before platform flows finalize
Breaking interaction changes use deprecation and migration rather than silent instance updates
non_goals: Custom controls where a native semantic control suffices
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and components library. Navigation, action and form teams use separate component sets and converge through shared state and token contracts.
definition_of_done: All component families and platform variants published
Accessibility, Security, Content and UX Engineering approvals recorded
State, validation and interaction tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Design money, data display, collection and visualization components
items.outcome: Every amount, debt result, transaction, list, table, chart and derivation uses one semantics-first component contract that preserves precision, provenance and accessible alternatives.
items.context: Visual inconsistency can turn a correct integer amount into an ambiguous or misleading decision. Charts, totals and projected figures need explicit semantics rather than cosmetic reuse.
scope: Amount, balance, delta, percentage, rate, payoff date, confidence, provenance and derivation primitives
Transaction, account, debt, goal, holding, split, household and audit record patterns
List, timeline, table, pagination, search, filter, sort, selection, bulk action and comparison
Trend, categorical spend, debt trajectory, scenario comparison, composition and progress visualization
Partial, zero, unavailable, stale, pending, projected, redacted and overflow variants
acceptance_criteria: Currency and source are visible for every consequential amount and mixed-currency totals are impossible without an approved conversion
Every chart has a text or table equivalent using the same server values and ordering
Projected, partial, stale, reversed and unconfirmed data cannot be mistaken for confirmed current values
Tables define keyboard, screen-reader, responsive and virtualized behavior before implementation
Derivation access is consistent and discoverable for every computed financial figure
contracts_schema: Display component properties reference MinorUnitAmount, provenance, confidence, freshness, completeness and derivation contract fields
security_privacy: Components support privacy masking, redaction and aggregate-only views without layout leaks
Examples use synthetic values and no merchant or account identifiers from production
observability: Missing currency/provenance, chart-table divergence, overflow, stale-data and derivation-open rates
tests: Virtualized table keyboard and screen-reader specification review
rollout_rollback: Publish primitives before platform high-fidelity flows
Rollback pins consumers to the prior component version and preserves data semantics
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and components library. Money primitives are frozen by the Design Systems Lead and money-path reviewer before platform composition.
definition_of_done: Financial and collection component families published
Money-path, Accessibility, Content and UX Engineering approvals recorded
Semantic, parity and privacy variants tested
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Design feedback, overlay, trust, consent and security components
items.outcome: Errors, status, permissions, consent, sharing, access, step-up and destructive decisions use consistent components that make risk, scope, recovery and authority explicit.
items.context: The highest-risk states appear across platforms. If each team invents banners, dialogs or approval affordances, denial can leak data and dangerous actions can look routine.
scope: Skeleton, progress, inline error, banner, snackbar, empty, offline, stale, degraded, retry, undo and success
Dialog, alert, sheet/drawer, popover, tooltip, date picker and focus/escape/back behavior
Permission rationale, consent, disclosure, grant, access log, privacy mask and safe exit
Step-up, approval chain, provenance, SLA clock, redaction, unmask and break-glass
Destructive, irreversible, cooling-off, revoked and recovery states
acceptance_criteria: Every T-UX-01 state has required, forbidden and recovery content plus platform adaptations
Consent and grant components show purpose, scope, duration, consequence and withdrawal before acceptance
Authorization denial reveals no hidden resource and never offers an ineligible bypass
Overlays restore focus or Back state, escape containers and never trap assistive technology
High-risk actions use purpose-built flows with provenance and diff rather than a generic modal
contracts_schema: State, permission, consent, grant, approval, denial, expiry and audit component properties map to published enums
security_privacy: Components default to least disclosure and safe failure
Coercion and shoulder-surfing variants include discreet exit, concealment and neutral notifications
observability: State exposure, retry, undo, denial, abandoned consent, approval expiry and focus failure events without content
tests: Focus, escape, Back and screen-reader overlay specifications
rollout_rollback: Security components require independent review before publication
Rollback disables a risky action or pins the prior component; it never falls back to a generic confirmation
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs and components library. Trust/security components require Design Systems, Security, Content and Accessibility co-review before platform use.
definition_of_done: Feedback, overlay and trust component families published
Security, Privacy, Accessibility and Content approvals recorded
Denial, coercion, focus and recovery tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Specify adaptive layout, themes, motion, haptics and reduced-motion behavior
items.outcome: Platform teams share explicit layout, theme and motion behavior while Android, customer web and admin retain native information density and interaction conventions.
items.context: Responsive behavior is structural, not a late breakpoint patch. Dark mode, high contrast, large text and reduced motion must influence components and flows before screen approval.
scope: Android compact, medium and expanded window classes, insets, IME and posture
Customer-web and admin grid, navigation, table and content-density breakpoints
Light, dark, high-contrast and dynamic-color policy
Largest text, 200 percent zoom, reflow, touch target and pointer/keyboard behavior
Motion duration/easing, state transitions, haptic roles and reduced-motion substitutions
acceptance_criteria: No approved screen is a stretched compact layout or a clipped desktop table at narrow width
Every token and component resolves in light, dark and high-contrast modes
Largest Android text and 200 percent web zoom preserve task completion without two-dimensional scrolling except data tables
Motion conveys state, meets performance budgets and has a reduced or instant alternative
Haptics never carry meaning without visual and accessible feedback
contracts_schema: Breakpoint, window class, density, theme, motion and haptic semantic records consumed by platform files
security_privacy: Privacy masks and redactions remain effective across themes and responsive rearrangement
Motion never reveals hidden content during transition
observability: Layout overflow, theme token gap, reduced-motion use, text-scale failure and breakpoint-specific task failure
tests: Window-class, zoom, text-scale and theme matrix
Responsive table and overlay containment fixtures
rollout_rollback: Publish behavior contracts before high-fidelity platform screens
Rollback pins prior layout/motion version and does not remove accessibility modes
non_goals: Forcing identical density on consumer and operator products
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Responsive, theme and motion specialists own separate specifications and platform leads verify adaptation in their files.
definition_of_done: Adaptive, theme and motion contracts published
Android, Web, Admin, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
Full matrix and reduced-motion tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Publish the product glossary, voice and regulated content patterns
items.outcome: Every platform uses one understandable, non-shaming and legally governed language system for money, debt, states, permissions, AI, sharing, billing, support and operator actions.
items.context: Inconsistent terms can make users misread debt, projections, access or reversals. Regulated and security copy must be versioned, while ordinary product copy still needs a coherent voice.
scope: Canonical financial, debt, transaction, sharing, AI, billing, rights and operator glossary
Voice principles, reading level, sentence and number conventions and prohibited shame/hype/advice patterns
Empty, loading, error, stale, denied, destructive, success and recovery copy templates
Consent, permission, disclaimer, plan change, refund, deletion, access and incident approval workflow
Minimum, typical and maximum content ranges with source-of-copy ownership
acceptance_criteria: A term has one definition and preferred label across Android, web, admin, contracts and support
Copy states source, status, consequence, safe remainder and next action without inventing a cause
Debt and correction language never shames, guarantees or disguises uncertainty
Regulated/security copy has version, reviewer, effective date, expiry and fail-closed behavior
Comprehension testing covers payoff, projected, available, pending, reversed, aggregate and revoked terms
contracts_schema: Glossary, message key, state, content range, regulated-copy version and approval records
security_privacy: Messages never echo raw content, credentials, hidden resource identity or operator identity where prohibited
Neutral safe-exit and notification copy is available for shared-device and coercive contexts
observability: Unknown term, copy-version mismatch, comprehension failure and support contact caused by wording
rollout_rollback: Publish source strings before platform flow finalization
Rollback pins the prior approved copy version and never substitutes local text
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Content Design owns glossary and source copy; Legal/Compliance approve governed strings and platform designers consume keys.
definition_of_done: Glossary, voice and content patterns merged
Content, Compliance, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
Lint, expiry and comprehension tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Define localization, pseudo-localization and bidirectional content readiness
items.outcome: Layouts, components, source copy and test fixtures are ready for approved Indian languages and bidirectional expansion before screens hardcode English dimensions or word order.
items.context: Translation after layout approval creates truncation and inaccessible rework. The initial language set remains a product decision, but every surface can be made localization-ready now.
scope: Language decision input covering user evidence, support and regulatory feasibility
Message keys, plural, gender, date, number, currency and list formatting rules
Pseudo-localization expansion, diacritic, missing-key and mirrored-layout fixtures
Icon/text ordering, charts, tables, screenshots and asset localization
Translator context, review, versioning and fallback behavior
acceptance_criteria: Every user-visible string is represented by a source key with context and owner
Pseudo-localization at maximum expansion produces no clipped action or hidden consequence
Currency and number formatting uses locale rules without changing stored value or currency
Bidirectional fixtures preserve logical reading and data ordering where supported
Missing or expired regulated translations fail closed to an approved fallback
contracts_schema: Locale, message key, plural variables, formatting role, translation version and approval records
security_privacy: Localization files contain no secrets or live user content
Fallback never removes a consent, warning or destructive consequence
observability: Missing key, fallback, truncation, locale-format and translation-version mismatch counts
rollout_rollback: Ship framework and pseudo locale before production translations
Rollback disables an incomplete locale while preserving approved source language
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Localization owns source-key and fixture contracts; platform teams test layout, and translators work in versioned locale files.
definition_of_done: Localization readiness and pseudo-locale specifications published
Content, Localization, Accessibility and platform approvals recorded
Expansion, bidi and number tests pass
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Publish the design-to-code handoff and conformance contract
items.outcome: A D6 artifact gives an implementation agent everything needed to build and test a screen without guessing layout, behavior, content, contracts, states, accessibility or assets.
items.context: A Figma link without version, component mapping, state table or contract fields is not a handoff. Three frontend repositories need one definition of implementation readiness and drift.
scope: Handoff checklist for flow, screen, component, state, data range, interaction, responsive, accessibility, content and telemetry
Figma version and frame IDs, asset manifest, token package and component mapping
API/contract fields, authorization, freshness, errors and synthetic fixtures per screen
Code Connect or equivalent source mapping and approved platform divergence
Design-to-code screenshot, semantic and interaction conformance evidence
acceptance_criteria: Every frontend ticket cites an immutable D6 artifact version and exact screen/flow IDs
Every screen handoff includes all applicable states, realistic content ranges and contract fields
Every component maps to a published library item and intended code component or records a reviewed gap
Assets include license, format, density, theme and accessibility metadata
A cold implementation reviewer can derive automated test IDs and acceptance scenarios without asking the designer
contracts_schema: schema/handoff-manifest.schema.json links immutable artifact/frame version, screens, flows, components, designed/inherited/exempt states, contract version, fixtures, assets, implementation tickets, QA scenarios, approvals, expiry and checksum
security_privacy: Handoff fixtures are synthetic and least-disclosing
Sensitive designs and exports follow Figma access and retention policy
observability: Missing handoff field, unmapped component, design drift, approved deviation and stale artifact counts
tests: Design-to-code screenshot and semantic baseline generation
rollout_rollback: D6 is required before frontend Ready; existing tickets remain Backlog until mapped
A handoff change creates a new version and reopens only affected implementation dependencies
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. UX Engineering owns the handoff schema and mappings; platform squads own manifests for their screens and implementation teams consume pinned versions.
definition_of_done: Handoff schema, template and conformance checks merged
Android, web and admin pilot handoffs pass cold-start review
UX Engineering, QA, Accessibility and CDO approvals recorded
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges
